```json
{
  "design": "Fuzzy regression discontinuity design (RDD)",
  "instrument": "Crossing the eligibility score cutoff of 70 (score >= 70), which sharply raises the probability of participation but does not deterministically assign treatment",
  "estimand": "Local average treatment effect (LATE) at the cutoff for compliers — i.e., the effect of participation for individuals whose enrollment status changes because of crossing the threshold",
  "global_generalization": "No. The estimate is local to the score cutoff and to compliers; it does not automatically generalize to people far from the threshold or to always-takers/never-takers",
  "assumptions": [
    "Continuity: potential outcomes (and all individual characteristics) vary smoothly through the score of 70 absent treatment",
    "No precise manipulation: individuals cannot exactly manipulate their score around the cutoff, so treatment status is as good as random near 70",
    "Relevance/first stage: crossing the cutoff has a significant, discontinuous effect on participation (supported by the observed jump)",
    "Exclusion restriction: crossing the cutoff affects employment outcomes only through program participation (no other channels)",
    "Monotonicity: crossing the cutoff weakly increases the probability of participation for everyone (no defiers)",
    "No other concurrent policy changes or discontinuities at the score of 70"
  ]
}
```
message.reasoning: Sharp vs fuzzy: participation jumps but not universal above, some below participate → fuzzy RDD. Instrument: crossing the score cutoff (score ≥ 70). Estimand: LATE / CACE for compliers at the cutoff (local average treatment effect at the threshold). Global generalization: no, only local to cutoff. Assumptions: continuity of potential outcomes at cutoff, no precise manipulation of score, exclusion restriction (only effect via participation), monotonicity (no defiers), no other concurrent changes at threshold, first stage relevance.
